# mathlib4

![GitHub CI](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/actions/workflows/build.yml/badge.svg?branch=master)
[![Bors enabled](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/bors-ng/bors-ng.github.io/refs/heads/master/images/badge_small.svg)](https://mathlib-bors-ca18eefec4cb.herokuapp.com/repositories/16)
[![project chat](https://img.shields.io/badge/zulip-join_chat-brightgreen.svg)](https://leanprover.zulipchat.com)
[![Gitpod Ready-to-Code](https://img.shields.io/badge/Gitpod-ready--to--code-blue?logo=gitpod)](https://gitpod.io/#https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4)

[Mathlib](https://leanprover-community.github.io) is a user maintained library for the [Lean theorem prover](https://leanprover.github.io).
It contains both programming infrastructure and mathematics,
as well as tactics that use the former and allow to develop the latter.

## Installation

You can find detailed instructions to install Lean, mathlib, and supporting tools on [our website](https://leanprover-community.github.io/get_started.html).
Alternatively, click on one of the buttons below to open a GitHub Codespace or a Gitpod workspace containing the project.

[![Open in GitHub Codespaces](https://github.com/codespaces/badge.svg)](https://codespaces.new/leanprover-community/mathlib4)

[![Open in Gitpod](https://gitpod.io/button/open-in-gitpod.svg)](https://gitpod.io/#https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4)

## Using `mathlib4` as a dependency

Please refer to
[https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/wiki/Using-mathlib4-as-a-dependency](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/wiki/Using-mathlib4-as-a-dependency)

## Experimenting

Got everything installed? Why not start with the [tutorial project](https://leanprover-community.github.io/install/project.html)?

For more pointers, see [Learning Lean](https://leanprover-community.github.io/learn.html).

## Documentation

Besides the installation guides above and [Lean's general
documentation](https://docs.lean-lang.org/lean4/doc/), the documentation
of mathlib consists of:

- [The mathlib4 docs](https://leanprover-community.github.io/mathlib4_docs/index.html): documentation [generated
  automatically](https://github.com/leanprover/doc-gen4) from the source `.lean` files.
- A description of [currently covered theories](https://leanprover-community.github.io/theories.html),
  as well as an [overview](https://leanprover-community.github.io/mathlib-overview.html) for mathematicians.
- Some [extra Lean documentation](https://leanprover-community.github.io/learn.html) not specific to mathlib (see "Miscellaneous topics")
- Documentation for people who would like to [contribute to mathlib](https://leanprover-community.github.io/contribute/index.html)

Much of the discussion surrounding mathlib occurs in a [Zulip chat
room](https://leanprover.zulipchat.com/), and you are welcome to join, or read
along without signing up.  Questions from users at all levels of expertise are
welcome!  We also provide an [archive of the public
discussions](https://leanprover-community.github.io/archive/), which is useful
for quick reference.

## Contributing

The complete documentation for contributing to ``mathlib`` is located
[on the community guide contribute to mathlib](https://leanprover-community.github.io/contribute/index.html)

You may want to subscribe to the `mathlib4` channel on [Zulip](https://leanprover.zulipchat.com/) to introduce yourself and your plan to the community.
Often you can find community members willing to help you get started and advise you on the fit and
feasibility of your project.

* To obtain precompiled `olean` files, run `lake exe cache get`. (Skipping this step means the next step will be very slow.)
* To build `mathlib4` run `lake build`.
* To build and run all tests, run `lake test`.
* You can use `lake build Mathlib.Import.Path` to build a particular file, e.g. `lake build Mathlib.Algebra.Group.Defs`.
* If you added a new file, run the following command to update `Mathlib.lean`

  ```shell
  lake exe mk_all
  ```

### Guidelines

Mathlib has the following guidelines and conventions that must be followed

 - The [style guide](https://leanprover-community.github.io/contribute/style.html)
 - A guide on the [naming convention](https://leanprover-community.github.io/contribute/naming.html)
 - The [documentation style](https://leanprover-community.github.io/contribute/doc.html)

### Downloading cached build files

You can run `lake exe cache get` to download cached build files that are computed by `mathlib4`'s automated workflow.

If something goes mysteriously wrong,
you can try one of `lake clean` or `rm -rf .lake` before trying `lake exe cache get` again.
In some circumstances you might try `lake exe cache get!`
which re-downloads cached build files even if they are available locally.

Call `lake exe cache` to see its help menu.

### Building HTML documentation

The [mathlib4_docs repository](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4_docs)
is responsible for generating and publishing the
[mathlib4 docs](https://leanprover-community.github.io/mathlib4_docs/index.html).

That repo can be used to build the docs locally:
```shell
git clone https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4_docs.git
cd mathlib4_docs
cp ../mathlib4/lean-toolchain .
lake exe cache get
lake build Mathlib:docs
```
The last step may take a while (>20 minutes).
The HTML files can then be found in `.lake/build/doc`.

## Transitioning from Lean 3

For users familiar with Lean 3 who want to get up to speed in Lean 4 and migrate their existing
Lean 3 code we have:

- A [survival guide](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/wiki/Lean-4-survival-guide-for-Lean-3-users)
  for Lean 3 users
- [Instructions to run `mathport`](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathport#running-on-a-project-other-than-mathlib)
  on a project other than mathlib. `mathport` is the tool the community used to port the entirety
  of `mathlib` from Lean 3 to Lean 4.

### Dependencies

If you are a mathlib contributor and want to update dependencies, use `lake update`,
or `lake update batteries aesop` (or similar) to update a subset of the dependencies.
This will update the `lake-manifest.json` file correctly.
You will need to make a PR after committing the changes to this file.

Please do not run `lake update -Kdoc=on` as previously advised, as the documentation related
dependencies should only be included when CI is building documentation.

Thank you again for joining our community.

payload.author: NoahW314
payload.body: My understanding was that we try to avoid having definitions with hypotheses since they are harder to work with.  So what's the motivation for this change?  The docstring seems to agree with the existing definition: it's the coefficient at *an* inverse image, which doesn't suggest injectivity.  While I agree that most uses of `leadingCoeff D` will have `D.Injective` as a hypothesis anyway, I'm not sure that's a good enough reason to change the definition.

payload.author: Hagb
payload.body:
> it's the coefficient at _an_ inverse image, which doesn't suggest injectivity

Thank you. I don't know why I just ignored the second sentence that it is an inverse image... I will edit the description.

> So what's the motivation for this change?

[`Function.invFun`](https://leanprover-community.github.io/mathlib4_docs/Mathlib/Logic/Function/Basic.html#Function.invFun) chooses an inverse image by applying `Exists.choose` (which is defined by `Classical.choose`) to `∃ x : α, D x = y`. If I understand correctly, `x` chosen from `∃ x : α, D x = y` and `g z` where `z` is chosen from `∃ x : α, D (g x) = y` generally cannot be proved equal or proved unequal if `D` has more than one inverse images from `y`.
```lean4
noncomputable def invFun {α : Sort u} {β} [Nonempty α] (D : α → β) : β → α :=
  open scoped Classical in
  fun y ↦ if h : (∃ x, D x = y) then h.choose else Classical.arbitrary α
  -- for readability I change the variable name `f` to `D` here.

noncomputable def AddMonoidAlgebra.leadingCoeff [Nonempty A] (f : R[A]) : R :=
  f (D.invFun <| f.supDegree D)
```
In `leadingCoeff`, this seems unnatural especially when `g` is `· + something`. Consider `A := σ →₀ ℕ`, `D := Finsupp.sum fun _ e ↦ e` i.e. sum of exponents of variables in a monomial, (then `supDegree D f` is the [total degree](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Degree_of_a_polynomial#Extension_to_polynomials_with_two_or_more_variables) of `f`). It cannot be proved that `(f * X a).leadingCoeff D = f.leadingCoeff D` without extra hypothesis like the `D.Injective` (or weaker ones). But my intuition was that we would hope that our "leading coeff" has similar positive property without extra hypothesis?

In general, `leadingCoeff_mul` needs `hD` even if not required by the definition of `leadingCoeff`.
```lean4
lemma leadingCoeff_mul [NoZeroDivisors R]
    (hD : D.Injective) (hadd : ∀ a1 a2, D (a1 + a2) = D a1 + D a2) :
    (p * q).leadingCoeff D = p.leadingCoeff D * q.leadingCoeff D
```

> My understanding was that we try to avoid having definitions with hypotheses since they are harder to work with.

Yes, probably. My motivation was more about intuition than engineering. I am okay with whatever the final status of this PR will become.

edit: `f` is `+` -> `g` is `· + something`
edit2: my situation -> my motivation

### 🚨 PR Title Needs Formatting
Please update the title to match our [commit style conventions](https://leanprover-community.github.io/contribute/commit.html).

Errors from script:
```
error: the PR title does not contain a colon
```

<details>
<summary>Details on the required title format</summary>

The title should fit the following format:
```
<kind>(<optional-scope>): <subject>
```
`<kind>` is:

- `feat` (feature)
- `fix` (bug fix)
- `doc` (documentation)
- `style` (formatting, missing semicolons, ...)
- `refactor`
- `test` (when adding missing tests)
- `chore` (maintain)
- `perf` (performance improvement, optimization, ...)
- `ci` (changes to continuous integration, repo automation, ...)

`<optional-scope>` is a name of module or a directory which contains changed modules.
This is not necessary to include, but may be useful if the `<subject>` is insufficient.
The `Mathlib` directory prefix is always omitted.
For instance, it could be

- Data/Nat/Basic
- Algebra/Group/Defs
- Topology/Constructions

`<subject>` has the following constraints:

- do not capitalize the first letter
- no dot(.) at the end
- use imperative, present tense: "change" not "changed" nor "changes"
</details>

payload.author: Hagb
payload.body:
I have some doubts:

`MvPolynomial.supDegree D f` is def-eq to `AddMonoidAlgebra.supDegree D f`. And most of these theorems stated in `MvPolynomial.supDegree` are proved directly by their counterpart stated in `AddMonoidAlgebra.supDegree`. For example, `MvPolynomial.ne_zero_of_supDegree_ne_bot` is proved in such way:
```lean4
theorem ne_zero_of_supDegree_ne_bot : p.supDegree D ≠ ⊥ → p ≠ 0 :=
    AddMonoidAlgebra.ne_zero_of_supDegree_ne_bot
```

1. Is it better to define `MvPolynomial.supDegree` and provide theorems stated in `MvPolynomial.supDegree` than use `AddMonoidAlgebra`'s?
2. Is there any way to create and maintain them without manually copying and specializing the statement in `AddMonoidAlgebra`?

payload.author: dagurtomas
payload.body: This is fine if you want explicit kernels in `Pointed`, but the `HasKernels` instance should be deduced from a general `HasLimits` instance. It seems like we don't have that, the way to go is to prove that the forgetful functor creates limits and use [`hasLimits_of_hasLimits_createsLimits`](https://leanprover-community.github.io/mathlib4_docs/Mathlib/CategoryTheory/Limits/Creates.html#CategoryTheory.hasLimits_of_hasLimits_createsLimits)

payload.author: dagurtomas
payload.body: You should move the file `Pointed.lean` into a new folder `Pointed`, rename it to `Basic.lean`, and create a new file `Limits.lean` where you develop the API for limits and colimits. If you're not in a rush with this, I would recommend developing the general limit/colimit API first and then start specialized work like this. But it would also be fine to just add this for now and add a TODO for the general stuff. But it should go in a new file, that also avoids the import increase

payload.author: CRudrum
payload.body:
Hi Dagur, thank you very much for your feedback! I agree that it makes sense to start with `Basic.lean` and `Limits.lean` files. I think I suggested a similar approach in [my introduction on Zulip](https://leanprover.zulipchat.com/#narrow/channel/113489-new-members/topic/Corijn.20Rudrum), but based on the advice I received there I decided to proceed in this way, just adding a `HasKernels` instance to the same file. Now I'm a bit unsure what to do. Putting my code in a separate file is of course no problem.

I'm not in a hurry with anything (Lean related). The main thing I would like to do is make it easier to work with pointed sets in Lean. I am very much open to suggestions on the best way to do that!

payload.author: Garmelon
payload.body:
> I did a search for `runLinter` and found a few under `scripts/bench`: is it worth changing those too? https://github.com/search?q=repo%3Aleanprover-community%2Fmathlib4%20runlinter&type=code cc: @Garmelon

Not sure. We're already building runLint manually so that the build doesn't get included in the lint measurements. If we `lake lint` instead of `lake exe runLint`, then it becomes less obvious why we `lake build runLint` beforehand.

Also, if `runLint` is ever renamed or replaced, then the current bench setup will crash and burn (good) instead of silently including the build time in the lint runtime (bad).

payload.author: bryangingechen
payload.body: OK, I guess we can leave bench alone then.

If they can then I don't know the syntax.

payload.author: SnirBroshi
payload.body:
> Why this `local instance : PartialOrder _ := ... in ` pattern?

`decidableEqOfDecidableLE`/`decidableLTOfDecidableLE` require `PartialOrder` and they're not able to use the one being built inside the `LinearOrder` instance (unlike when they were default values, for some reason), so creating a `PartialOrder` beforehand fixes it.

As to why `local ... in ...`, I'm afraid of diamonds so I want these intermediate instances to be as private as possible.
I have no clue what `in` means here though, it doesn't seem to scope the `local instance` attribute. But it's valid syntax 😅
There are existing types with a `PartialOrder` instance before `LinearOrder`, not sure how it avoids diamonds.

payload.author: thorimur
payload.body:
Hmm, I kind of think that namespacing under the theorem is good. There isn't a topic called `ExistsCardinalDirected`, and these definitions are specifically intended to refer to the final theorem, correct? The theorem declaration's name accurately points to the organizing principle when used as a namespace, so I'm not clear on why we need to rename it.

(I've mentioned this on Zulip but wanted to also mention it here. :) )

payload.author: vihdzp
payload.body: Namespacing under a proof seems non-idiomatic to me, since it won't actually enable any sort of dot notation. I think we should either put the auxiliary theorems in the same namespace as the final theorem, or simply make them private.

payload.author: thorimur
payload.body:
Hmm...I'm not quite convinced by the dot-notation reasoning per se, since namespaces aren't just for dot notation, they're for organization too. And it seems that the organization here is "are constructed for this theorem".

But after some thought I do think I agree with the next statement, and making them private makes sense to me! Can we try that? :) (Likewise, if they might really be used publicly then I suspect that indeed means that organizing them under the theorem is not really conceptually appropriate in the first place, and so they'd deserve a more general organizing location...)

More generally, is any of this written down anywhere? As far as I can see the style guide/naming conventions is largely silent on naming namespaces in general. Am I missing any mentions of it? If not we should probably reach consensus on zulip (has this already happened?) and fix that 😁

payload.author: SnirBroshi
payload.body:
Everything here can be made `private`, but unfortunately there's no way to properly deprecate these names.
[#mathlib4 > Deprecation on the way from public to private](https://leanprover.zulipchat.com/#narrow/channel/287929-mathlib4/topic/Deprecation.20on.20the.20way.20from.20public.20to.20private/with/596323960)

Probably no.

payload.body: Hey, could you give some motivation for adding these definitions? What are some interesting results you plan to prove with them?

payload.author: akiezun
payload.body: The main motivation was that analyzing looking at ~year, a few thousand, of recent math.NT papers, I see 'almost prime' as a common (66 papers since 2025) elementary term that is easily expressible in Mathlib but absent in the library. Adding it centrally will help people formalize their results. I myself do not have a specific bigger theorem in mind yet.

payload.author: vihdzp
payload.body: Can you cite some examples? I haven't heard of "almost primes" before (though I have heard of semiprimes, and IMO it could be nice having this as an auxiliary definition for them).

payload.author: akiezun
payload.body:
2501.18048 (https://arxiv.org/abs/2501.18048), Adrian W. Dudek; Daniel R. Johnston. Almost primes between all squares
 
 2601.15564 (https://arxiv.org/abs/2601.15564), Daniel R. Johnston; Jonathan P. Sorenson; Simon N. Thomas; Jonathan E. Webster. Primes and almost primes between cubes
 
 2503.21490 (https://arxiv.org/abs/2503.21490), Tsz Ho Chan. Almost cubes and fourth powers in short intervals
 
 2506.21642 (https://arxiv.org/abs/2506.21642), Cécile Dartyge; Joël Rivat; Cathy Swaenepoel. Prime numbers with an almost prime reverse

### 🚨 PR Title Needs Formatting
Please update the title to match our [commit style conventions](https://leanprover-community.github.io/contribute/commit.html).

Errors from script:
```
error: the PR title does not contain a colon
```

<details>
<summary>Details on the required title format</summary>

The title should fit the following format:
```
<kind>(<optional-scope>): <subject>
```
`<kind>` is:

- `feat` (feature)
- `fix` (bug fix)
- `doc` (documentation)
- `style` (formatting, missing semicolons, ...)
- `refactor`
- `test` (when adding missing tests)
- `chore` (maintain)
- `perf` (performance improvement, optimization, ...)
- `ci` (changes to continuous integration, repo automation, ...)

`<optional-scope>` is a name of module or a directory which contains changed modules.
This is not necessary to include, but may be useful if the `<subject>` is insufficient.
The `Mathlib` directory prefix is always omitted.
For instance, it could be

- Data/Nat/Basic
- Algebra/Group/Defs
- Topology/Constructions

`<subject>` has the following constraints:

- do not capitalize the first letter
- no dot(.) at the end
- use imperative, present tense: "change" not "changed" nor "changes"
</details>
<!-- Sticky Pull Request CommentPR Title Check -->
